title: [22/22] Deployment process — CI gate, deploy.sh, releases with atomic symlink flip
body:
**Blocked by:** #29, #40

## Context

Every previous issue built software or infrastructure; this last issue (22 of 22) builds the process that gets that software onto the server — and keeps it off the server by any other path. The motivating history is written into the specification itself: an earlier, real, working `backend/` directory existed in the planning repository, written against an older 11-section (and, in hindsight, incomplete) version of the specification, and it had to be discarded wholesale as a source of truth because it grew in parallel with documentation that was still being formed. Its copy still serves as reference code for verifying decisions; nothing is written against it anymore.

The process below is the direct response to that lesson: the Semprec implementation lives in its own GitHub repository (this one — separate from the local, remote-less `vize/` planning repo), and **nothing reaches the server that did not pass commit → test → tag → deploy**. No manual edits on the running production checkout, ever.

Issue #40 (Operations) provisioned the server: `provision.sh` created the bare `/opt/semprec` directory tree (`releases/`, `shared/`, …), the systemd units, and `/opt/semprec/shared/.env` with bootstrap secrets. This issue delivers everything that flows through that tree: branch protection and the CI gate on GitHub, semantic version tags, `deploy.sh` with the release/symlink mechanics, the rollback rule, and the migration discipline that makes rollback safe.

## Task

Implement the development and deployment process as six decided pieces:

**1. GitHub as the implementation remote, separate from the planning repo**

The `vize/` planning repository (documentation, mock, the specification page) stays what it is — local, no remote, its own per-repo-root CLAUDE.md — because it solves a different problem (planning and decision review, not operating code). The actual Semprec implementation (the monorepo with `packages/`/`modules/`/`services/`) lives in its own, new GitHub repository, founded only once the specification was complete enough to build against without repeating the earlier mistake — not as a continuation of the old, deleted `backend/` directory.

**2. Trunk-based development — `main` always deployable, protected, merge only via PR with green CI**

No `develop`/release branch model on top — for one self-hosted server with one primary developer that would be complexity with no matching benefit (the same logic used elsewhere to reject a delegation concurrency cap). `main` is the only long-lived branch and always represents a state that could safely be deployed: branch protection on GitHub, no direct pushes, commits land only through a pull request that passed CI (below) before merging. Short-lived feature branches come and go freely — their names/conventions do not matter.

**3. Semantic version tag on `main` — one version for the whole monorepo, not per package**

A `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` git tag on the `main` commit that is what gets deployed. One version for the entire monorepo, never independent versions per `packages/`/`modules/`/`services/` — independent versioning makes sense for a library published to outside consumers (exactly the pi-agent-core case), not for a single internally deployed whole where all five systemd processes always run from the same commit anyway. Distinguishing major/minor/patch enforces nothing by itself (no third-party API a breaking change could break) — it is readable history for a human, not an enforcement mechanism.

**4. CI gate — the three test tiers run on every push; a tag may only be cut from a green commit**

Nothing new to design — issue #29 already decided the testing strategy (unit tests, integration tests against an ephemeral Postgres, a small set of e2e scenarios). This piece wires it in: GitHub Actions runs all three tiers on every push to a PR branch and on every merge to `main`. A tag (and therefore a deployment candidate) may only be created on a commit where that run passed — not as a separate pre-deploy check, but as a precondition of the tag itself. The same gate reuses the contract tests for pi-agent-core — the same CI runs, one test suite, not a separate pipeline alongside.

**5. Deployment = releases directory + atomic symlink flip, never overwriting a running checkout**

The rejected pattern is "SSH to the server, `git pull` in the directory the systemd services run from" — exactly what this process replaces. The problem is not only aesthetic: `git pull` into a running checkout is not atomic (a process mid-pull can briefly read a mix of old and new files), and rollback means a second manual `git checkout` under pressure instead of one fast action. The standard alternative (the same shape as the Capistrano/Kamal deploy pattern):

```
/opt/semprec/releases/v1.4.2/    -- fresh checkout of the tag, install, build
/opt/semprec/releases/v1.4.1/    -- previous release, stays on disk
/opt/semprec/current             -- symlink to the currently running release
/opt/semprec/shared/.env         -- root-owned bootstrap secrets outside the release dirs (issue #40)

deploy.sh v1.4.2:
  1. git clone --branch v1.4.2 <repo> releases/v1.4.2
  2. pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build
  3. run pending migrations (forward-only)
  4. ln -sfn releases/v1.4.2 current    -- atomic symlink swap
  5. systemctl restart semprec-api semprec-agents semprec-mailsync@* semprec-transcribe semprec-ai-gateway
```

Rollback is steps 4+5 with the previous version instead of the new one — no new build, no new checkout, just repointing the symlink and restarting the processes, which read from `current` anyway. The script is run manually for v1 (see Out of scope) — but it is a *script*, not a sequence of manual commands living in someone's head, so later automation means "run this same script from CI", not rewriting the mechanism.

**6. Code rollback is instant; schema rollback is not — which enforces backward-compatible migrations**

The symlink flip returns the code to the previous version in seconds. A migration that already ran against the database as part of a bad deploy is *not* undone by that step — migrations are forward-only by design, not by accident, so the rollback path does not even attempt to unwind schema. The consequence has to be upheld as a discipline in how migrations are written, not in the deploy script: migrations in one release must remain backward compatible with the old code one step back (add a column, do not make it mandatory for the old code yet; never rename/delete a column in the same release that stops using it — a two-step "expand, then later contract"). If a bug requires reverting schema, the answer is a new forward commit, never a migration rollback — the same "fix forward, never silently unwind" discipline enforced elsewhere in the system.

## Scope

### In scope

- Founding/configuring the GitHub implementation repository as the single remote for the monorepo, separate from the local planning repo.
- Branch protection on `main`: no direct pushes, merge only via pull request with a green CI run.
- The GitHub Actions workflow running the three test tiers from issue #29 (unit, integration against an ephemeral Postgres, e2e scenarios), including the pi-agent-core contract tests as part of the same suite, on every push to a PR branch and every merge to `main`.
- The tag discipline: `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tags on `main` only, cut only from commits with a passing CI run — enforced as the precondition of tagging, not as a separate pre-deploy check.
- `deploy.sh` in the implementation repo (alongside `provision.sh` from issue #40): checkout of the tag into `/opt/semprec/releases/<tag>/`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`, running pending forward-only migrations, the atomic `ln -sfn` flip of `/opt/semprec/current`, and restart of all five systemd services. Secrets are never part of a release — processes read `/opt/semprec/shared/.env` (via the systemd `EnvironmentFile=` mechanism from issue #40), which lives outside the release directories and survives every deploy.
- The rollback path: repoint `current` to the previous release directory still on disk and restart — documented and executable as the same script's fast path, with no rebuild and no schema unwinding.
- The expand/contract migration discipline as a written rule of the repository (migrations backward compatible one release back; two-step rename/delete; schema reverts happen as new forward commits).

### Out of scope

- **A fully automated pipeline (auto-deploy on tag push)** — considered and deliberately deferred, not forgotten (the same logic as TOTP in auth and the sandbox layer in the agent runtime): before a first real running version of Semprec exists, building deployment automation solves a problem nobody has experienced yet. The mechanism above is designed so this later step is a small extension, not a rewrite: a GitHub Actions job (triggered on tag push, via a self-hosted runner on the server itself or SSH from a hosted runner) will one day call the very same `deploy.sh` a human runs manually today. What is being deferred is *when* automation switches on, not *how* — the *how* is decided now.
- Server provisioning, the systemd unit files, `shared/.env` contents, Caddy, backups — all delivered by issue #40; this issue only consumes the provisioned tree.
- The test tiers themselves — decided and built in issue #29; this issue only wires them into the gate.
- Down-migrations / reversible migrations — rejected; migrations stay forward-only.
- Per-package independent versioning of the monorepo — rejected (one version for the whole).
- A `develop`/release branching model — rejected (trunk-based only).

## Dependencies

- **Test strategy (#29)** — the three test tiers (unit, integration against ephemeral Postgres, e2e) and the pi-agent-core contract tests that the CI gate runs; without them the gate has nothing to enforce.
- **Operations/provisioning (#40)** — `provision.sh` creates the bare `/opt/semprec` directory tree (`releases/`, `shared/`, …), the systemd units with `EnvironmentFile=`, and the root-owned `shared/.env`; `deploy.sh` fills `releases/` and flips `current` on top of exactly that tree and must stay consistent with it.
- Implicitly, the forward-only migration mechanism and the five-process topology (`semprec-api`, `semprec-agents`, `semprec-mailsync@*`, `semprec-transcribe`, `semprec-ai-gateway`) whose services `deploy.sh` restarts.
- **No downstream issue** — last in the queue (22/22).

## Reference to the specification

`vize/backend.html`, lines 4868-5033 — section 13, "Vývojový a nasazovací proces" ("Git → test → deployment, not editing the running server — the lesson from what was already thrown away once"). Contains the decision blocks: "GitHub as the implementation remote, separate from the planning repository", "Trunk-based — main always deployable, protected, merge only via PR with green CI", "Semantic tag on main — one version for the whole monorepo, not per package", "CI gate — the three test tiers run on every push, a tag is cut only from a green commit", "Deployment = releases directory + atomic symlink flip, not overwriting the running checkout" (including the `deploy.sh` listing and the rollback rule), "Code rollback is instant, schema rollback is not — which enforces backward-compatible migrations", and the considered-and-deferred block "Fully automated pipeline (auto-deploy on tag push)".
